About this blog

A commonplace book, kept in public.

The Quiet Margin is written by Ava Whitfield, who writes about slow living, books and travel. It began as a private notebook — a place to keep half-finished thoughts, lines copied out of novels, and notes from walks — and it is still, at heart, exactly that.

There is nothing to buy here and nothing to sign up for except the occasional letter. Just essays, published when they are ready, and an open invitation to read them slowly.

— Ava Whitfield

About

Why a quiet margin?

Every book has margins — the white space around the words where readers argue, agree, underline and daydream. This blog lives in that space. The Quiet Margin is a personal blog: essays, travel notes, reading reflections and small observations from everyday life, published for the pleasure of writing them down properly.

What you'll find here

Essays on attention, rest and routine. Travel notes written slowly, mostly from trains and off-season towns. Thoughts on books and ideas — why we keep them, reread them, and lend them to friends. And dispatches from everyday life: kitchens, walks, letters, playlists, and the other small machinery of a life.

How it works

One piece a week, drafted by hand in a paper notebook before it ever meets a keyboard. There are no products, no services and no sponsors — just writing. If a piece stays with you, the kindest thing you can do is send it to one person who might like it too.

The blog is written by Ava Whitfield, who writes about slow living, books and travel.
